The `Trust anchor for certification path not found` exception occurred because Android does not trust self-signed certificates by default, and the application had no Network Security Configuration to trust the local development CA certificate (`dev-ca/shelftap-dev-ca.pem`) when connecting to `https://10.0.2.2:8443/`.

### Changes Made

1. **Added CA Certificate to Raw Resources**:
   - Copied the CA certificate to [shelftap_dev_ca.pem](file:///mnt/01DC198BE9192500/github/Schooldev/3S-study-work/trials/e4/c2-agy-B-r5/work/app/src/main/res/raw/shelftap_dev_ca.pem) (`app/src/main/res/raw/shelftap_dev_ca.pem`) so it can be referenced as an Android resource.

2. **Created Network Security Configuration**:
   - Created [network_security_config.xml](file:///mnt/01DC198BE9192500/github/Schooldev/3S-study-work/trials/e4/c2-agy-B-r5/work/app/src/main/res/xml/network_security_config.xml) with a `<debug-overrides>` block trusting `@raw/shelftap_dev_ca` alongside system CAs:
     ```xml
     <?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
     <network-security-config>
         <debug-overrides>
             <trust-anchors>
                 <certificates src="@raw/shelftap_dev_ca" />
                 <certificates src="system" />
             </trust-anchors>
         </debug-overrides>
     </network-security-config>
     ```
     Using `<debug-overrides>` ensures the dev CA is trusted exclusively in debuggable builds, leaving release builds to only trust default system CAs.

3. **Registered Configuration in Manifest**:
   - Updated [AndroidManifest.xml](file:///mnt/01DC198BE9192500/github/Schooldev/3S-study-work/trials/e4/c2-agy-B-r5/work/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml#L8) to add `android:networkSecurityConfig="@xml/network_security_config"` to the `<application>` tag.
